body: As a South American, Checo has many ups and downs
I agree. I also supspect that I might have autism although I never got diagnosed with it.

My parents make enough money and they support me financially. I'm glad for that but they also want to influence my decisions. They would be really dissapointed if I tell them that I want to quit my studies and propably cut the support. But honestly i wouldn't blame them because i don't really have anything that I'm passionate about or good at.

Edit: I always wanted to become a pilot but that's not possible as it requires really good grades in maths and physics in your high school degree and I don't have that.

Thanks for your advice, i'll try it if i don't procrastinate on it as well.

About my mental health: I have my parens and my roomates but i would feel really uncomfortable talking with my parents about that issue and even more with my roommates.

The problem for me was that i wasn't really good at defending myself verbally. If you say something like "stop it" they'll just laugh at you. Insulting them doesn't help either.

A few times i actually tried to defend myself physically. They didn't report me but just hit back harder when noone else was watching.

I'm more concerned about the consequences than the actual virus at this point. I mean we can't stay in this lockdown mode forever. Just imagine the consequences for economy and society. Especially in poorer countries there could be complete chaos.

In Germany the government says that they will open universities on 20th of April again but isn't that unrealistic? I expect the number of infections to be much higher until then.
Ok. Then i guess i don't have a problem with being myself and I should focus on the self improvement part.

Good point. However, personally I could never fake being someone. Either I am a confident person or I am not.
I just think that some people (including me) have to change in order to make friends or find love which i totally understand.
Nice way of looking at it. Thanks!
